newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-JOHNSON DOMINANT AS MARINERS BEAT ROCKIES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-JOHNSON DOMINANT AS MARINERS BEAT ROCKIES.

text.p: Seattle fireballer Randy Johnson, who has spent his career mowing down American League batters, got to show his stuff to some National League hitters on Friday.
Johnson (10-1) turned in his usual overpowering performance from the mound to lead the Mariners to a 6-1 thumping of the Colorado Rockies.
In Johnson's sixth consecutive win, he walked two and struck out 12, marking the 75th time he has reached double figures in strikeouts.
In his last four starts, Johnson has allowed one run and nine hits -- eight of them singles -- in 33 innings. He has walked nine and struck out 51 in pitching to a 0.27 ERA.
Johnson's 31-inning scoreless streak was snapped with two outs in the third when Eric Young homered to left field for the Rockies' only run.

Edgar Martinez had a solo homer and a two-run double for Seattle. Russ Davis added a solo shot and Ken Griffey and Jose Cruz each drove in a run for the Mariners, who won for the 10th time in their last 12 games.
Colorado starter Jamey Wright (4-4) gave up three runs and four hits over six innings for the loss.

In Oakland, Mike Piazza snapped a ninth-inning tie with an RBI double and Eric Karros hit a two-run homer and drove in three as the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the Athletics 6-4, gaining a split of their two-game interleague series.
Wilton Guerrero led off the top of the ninth with a double to right off Aaron Small (5-3) and scored on Piazza's double off the right-field wall for a 5-4 Dodgers' lead.
The Dodgers added an insurance run when Dane Johnson, who had relieved Small, walked Karros with the bases loaded to force home Todd Zeile, who had earlier drawn a base on balls.
With the Dodgers using a designated hitter in the lineup when playing in an American League park, Piazza went 5-for-9 in his first two games as a DH.
Darren Hall (1-2) got the win with one scoreless inning.
At Texas, Rusty Greer blasted his second homer of the game to lead off the ninth inning and lift the Rangers a 6-5 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The Rangers avenged Thursday's loss to San Francisco in what was the first interleague regular-season game in major league baseball history.
Rich Rodriguez (2-3) relieved Rod Beck to start the ninth and Greer sent a 2-1 pitch over the left-field wall. Greer also belted a two-run homer off Giants' starter Shawn Estes in the fifth inning.
Juan Gonzalez also smacked a two-run shot off Estes in the first inning. J.T. Snow and Barry Bonds had solo homers for the Giants.
John Wetteland (4-0) pitched a scoreless ninth to pick up the win for Texas.

In Anaheim, Quilvio Veras's double with two outs in the top of the 14th inning scored Greg Vaughn with the winning run as the San Diego Padres outlasted the Angels 8-7 in baseball's longest interleague game at five hours and three minutes.
Shigetoshi Hasegawa (1-4) started the 14th for Anaheim and retired his first two batters but walked Vaughn before Veras lined a 1-1 pitch off the wall in left-centre field for the winning hit.
Veras finished the night 4-for-7 with a run scored and Greg Vaughn and Wally Joyner homered for San Diego, which tied the game with three runs in the eighth inning.
Dave Hollins went 4-for-6 with a pair of RBI and two runs scored for the Angels.
Doug Bochtler (1-2) pitched two hitless innings to earn the win.
